sentences.text: The brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no. 1 had married to respondent no. 2 on 20.04.2011 at Delhi according to Muslim Rites and Ceremonies.
After the marriage, owing to temperamental differences, the relationship between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no.2 deteriorated and respondent no. 2 started living separately since April, 2013.

On complaint of respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no. 2281/2015was registered at Police Station Shakarpur, Delhi for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406/34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act against the petitioners.

It is stated that during the pendency of litigations, both the parties had amicably resolved their disputed before Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts,
Delhi vide Settlement Agreement dated 05.11.2022.
7.

On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled before Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi vide Settlement Agreement dated 05.11.2022 and affidavits showing the protection of interest of minor child as per the judgment titled as Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava, (2020) 20 SCC 787 passed by the Honble Supreme Court have been filed and the same are on record.

It is submitted that no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles, stridhan,
marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner no.1 and other family members.
9. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received all amounts and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

10. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

11. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 2281/2015, registered at Police Station Shakarpur, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
12.
The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J MAY 31, 2023/
